articles.authors: Andres Garcia Coleto, Henry Crawford-Eng, Theodore J. Dahl, Maya Shapiro, Maria Schnuck, Kyle J. Walsh, Steven T. Lipkowitz, Marcel W. Pruessner, Nathan F. Tyndall, Jacob N. Bouchard, Alin O. Antohe, Soumen Kar, Patrick O’Mullan, Cooper D. Hurley, Peter Hedlesky, Vijay S. S. Sundaram, Stefan F. Preble, Kevin A. McComber, James Eakin, Douglas T. Petkie et al.
articles.summary: Silicon‐photonics platforms operating at visible and near‐infrared wavelengths are essential for a growing range of applications, including biosensing, chemical detection, Raman spectroscopy, quantum, optogenetics, and displays. However, unlike their infrared counterparts, visible‐wavelength platforms have lacked comprehensive component libraries with pre‐characterized devices, limiting the ability to rapidly design photonic integrated circuits for these applications. …

articles.title: Tunable Optical-to-THz Frequency Conversion Driven by Localized Surface Phonon Polaritons in LiNbO3 Metasurfaces
articles.authors: C. McDonnell, M. Ferrera, F. Moia, V. Sajeev, M. Finazzi, A. Toma, C. De Angelis, M. Celebrano, T. Ellenbogen, L. Carletti
institutions: National Institute of Optics − National Research Council (INO−CNR)
articles.summary: We demonstrate tunable THz generation by optical rectification in LiNbO3 rod metasurfaces supporting localized surface phonon polaritons (LSPhPs). By varying the rod length, the LSPhP resonance is tuned across the 4–5 THz range, producing a systematic red-shift of the generated THz spectral peak. THz time-domain spectroscopy and numerical calculations show that the emitted spectrum is governed by the geometry-dependent LSPhP response. …

articles.title: Dual quasi-bound states in the continuum enabled non-dispersive infrared gas sensing
articles.authors: Hong-Chao Liu, Yibing Zhu, Zhi-Fan Li, Zhi-Hao Yan, Qian Wang, Wenbo Duan, Jie Sun, Ke-Sheng Shen, Qiong Gan Zhu, Shi-Qing Dong, Chao Dong, Hai Lu
articles.summary: In this paper, we demonstrate a symmetry-engineered dielectric metasurface supporting dual quasi-bound states in the continuum (QBICs) for mid-infrared narrowband emission and non-dispersive infrared (NDIR) gas sensing. By introducing rotational and non-centrosymmetric perturbations into an elliptical dimer, two high-Q resonances associated with symmetry-protected and Fabry–Pérot QBIC mechanisms are simultaneously realized within a single metasurface platform. The physical origins and electromagnetic characteristics of the two QBIC modes are elucidated through near-field field distributions, multipole decomposition, and coupled-mode analysis. …

articles.title: FRACTAL: A Ratiometric-based Fingerprinting Framework for Robust Spectral Classification and Ratio-based Spectroscopic Marker Discovery
articles.summary: Spectral classification is conventionally performed on band intensities, yet ratios between bands have long served as diagnostic indices in vibrational spectroscopy, from lipid-to-protein markers of membrane composition to amide ratios reporting protein secondary structure. Their use, however, has remained confined to a handful of expert-selected pairs, leaving most of the ratio information contained in a spectrum unexamined. Here I present FRACTAL (Full Ratio Combinatorial Analysis for Classification and Analytical Interpretation), which computes every pairwise log-intensity ratio among detected peaks to form a complete ratiometric fingerprint, grounded in compositional data analysis. …
